title: Microsoft Is Rewriting Windows 11's Oldest Dialogs in WinUI 3, Slowly
excerpt: Marcus Ash confirmed WinUI rewrites of Windows 11's leftover Win32 dialogs and MMC consoles are in progress, while 25 legacy tools — from Device Manager to Phone Dialer — still open today.
body:
• Microsoft design chief Marcus Ash confirmed his team is working on WinUI versions of Windows 11's leftover Win32 dialogs and MMC consoles, replying "Noted and working on that too" — with no timeline shared.
  • Windows Latest counted 25 legacy dialogs and tools you can still open today, from Device Manager (devmgmt.msc) and Disk Management to Mouse Properties (main.cpl) and the Phone Dialer.
  • Already moving: File and Folder Properties, the file copy dialog, a modern Run dialog, AutoPlay and Print Management have WinUI versions done or in testing.
  • Reader utility: nothing changes on your PC today — the legacy dialogs still open via the Run commands listed below, and the modern Run is opt-in in preview builds under Settings > System > Advanced.

Five years after Windows 11 launched, opening Device Manager next to the Settings app still feels like using two different operating systems. Microsoft now says, again and on the record, that it is working through that backlog: design chief Marcus Ash, Microsoft's CVP of Design and Research for Windows and Devices, replied to a user asking the company to modernise the legacy Win32 dialogs and MMC apps with "Noted and working on that too," according to Windows Latest. Ash shared no timeline.

What Microsoft has actually committed to

The November comment is the latest in a sequence Windows Latest has tracked. In March, Ash said the team was building tooling "to scale modernizing other dialogs." In May, Partner Director of Design March Rogers confirmed they are "working through our list of all older dialogs and rewriting them in WinUI 3," and in a separate May post Rogers said the file copy dialog is already done and the common file dialog is on the list. In July, Windows president Pavan Davuluri wrote that WinUI 3 had been extended into more of the Windows shell, naming the new Run experience, with AutoPlay and more File and Folder Properties dialogs coming to Insider builds. Microsoft calls WinUI 3 its recommended native UI framework for new desktop apps.

"We are working through our list of all older dialogs and rewriting them in WinUI 3."

— March Rogers, Partner Director of Design, Microsoft

25 you can still open today

Windows Latest's hands-on list runs to 25, each opened from Search or the Run box. They include Defragment and Optimize Drives (dfrgui), Mouse Properties (main.cpl), Sound (mmsys.cpl), Network Connections (ncpa.cpl), Power Options (powercfg.cpl), Programs and Features (appwiz.cpl), System Properties (sysdm.cpl), Folder Options, Desktop Icon Settings, Device Manager (devmgmt.msc), Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc), Services (services.msc), Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc), Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc), Computer Management (compmgmt.msc), Local Group Policy Editor (gpedit.msc), Character Map (charmap), Disk Cleanup (cleanmgr), ODBC Data Source Administrator (odbcad32), DirectX Diagnostic Tool (dxdiag), Bluetooth File Transfer (fsquirt) and the Format dialog — plus Sticky Keys and the Phone Dialer (dialer), a Windows 95-era app built for modem calls.

What is already rebuilt

Some of the worst offenders are moving first. The File Explorer Properties dialog has a WinUI 3 version with dark mode in testing, and Rogers says the file copy dialog is done. The modern Run dialog, written in C# and WinUI 3, posts a 94ms median time-to-show against 103ms for the legacy Run, and is opt-in under Settings > System > Advanced in preview builds. AutoPlay is getting its WinUI 3 redesign, Print Management has a WinUI 3 app in testing replacing its MMC console, and Reset this PC — still in Windows 8.1 design language — is next on the list. Even Sticky Keys shows the pattern: preview builds 26340.9882 and 26320.9876 add a "Never turn on Sticky Keys with this shortcut" checkbox, but the dialog itself kept its Win32 look.

Why this is slow

The hard parts are structural. MMC is a framework hosting snap-ins such as Device Manager, Services and Event Viewer, so each console must be rebuilt one at a time. Control Panel is trickier still: Rogers has said Microsoft is moving its controls into Settings carefully because of the many network and printer devices and drivers that must not break. Until then, Settings keeps sending users back to the old windows — which, for now, remain one Run command away.

March Rogers confirmed work on rewriting older dialogs.
Pavan Davuluri extended WinUI 3 into more Windows shell components.
